text:
sam_runtime: Quick note — observed a regression in end-to-end p95 on streaming endpoints after the last batching tweak. Looks tied to small-batch admission + KV prefetch interplay. attaching inline snapshot of profiler output below. :eyes:

lina_sre: Can you paste the profiler snippet here? I can look at traces.

sam_runtime: sure — main finding: when admission allows bursts of many tiny requests we trigger kernel fallback thrash. cheap summary:
```
path: streaming -> admission -> batch_coalesce
condition: incoming burst of 1-8 token requests (many)
batching: greedy coalesce with short window (2ms)
kv: prefetch enabled (async), misses spike ~3x
kernels: small-kernel chosen then fallback to generic -> extra memcpy/serialize
metric: p95 +50ms, cpu memcpy +40%, nvlink stalls +15%
```

miguel_ml: hmm. So small-window coalesce + async prefetch creates many partially-populated batches that then fall back to safe kernels? Are you seeing partial-decode scheduling delays too?

sam_runtime: yes — partial-decode queue gets a lot of items flagged for immediate flush. The runtime's partial-decode scheduling prioritizer then preempts larger decode tasks. It's basically thrashing between tiny-kernel fast paths and generic fallback that pay a big overhead.

zoe_infra: any change in token_budget targets recently? We tuned targets to be more permissive last week which may increase tiny-batch admits.

carla_eng: we did relax token budget to reduce latency for small chat messages. That could explain more tiny batches. But why kernel fallback? Shouldn't the small kernel handle it?

sam_runtime: two things: 1) kernel selection uses estimated tensor shapes based on batch occupancy at scheduling time; when prefetch hasn't filled KV yet, shape estimation flips to generic path. 2) the async KV prefetch sometimes returns after scheduler already chose kernel -> fallback path executed. Net effect: wasted work + stalls.

miguel_ml: idea: add a short admission hold-on-prefetch flag for tiny batches (e.g., if batch_size < 4 AND kv_prefetch_inflight, extend coalesce window by 1-2ms) — gives prefetch a chance and stabilizes kernel decision.

lina_sre: +1 but be careful with latency SLO. If we extend window, p50 might increase. Could we make it burst-aware: only extend when a burst pattern is detected (n reqs in last 10ms > threshold) so single small chat messages unaffected?

sam_runtime: that's what I was thinking — "burst-aware admission". heuristics:
- detect burst: sliding_count(10ms) >= 6
- if burst and batch_size predicted <=4 and kv_prefetch_inflight: coalesce_window += 1.5ms
- also mark these batches as "sticky" for kernel decision so we don't flip to fallback once prefetch arrives

carla_eng: how do we mark sticky? scheduler state across prefetch events? sounds invasive.

sam_runtime: small state: batch_id -> candidate_kernel cached until kernel commit or timeout(3ms). If prefetch completes and candidate_kernel still valid, commit that kernel; if commit not possible, fall back but suppress immediate partial-decode preempt for 1ms to avoid cascade.

zoe_infra: we should simulate in perf env before prod. I can spin up a job to replay production traces with the bursty pattern. If we add the extra wait, we should measure p50 and p95 separately and also check GPU occupancy.

miguel_ml: also consider introducing a KV staleness hint to the kernel selector: if prefetch_age < X ms prefer small kernel, else generic. That reduces flip.

lina_sre: good call. Quick experiment suggestion:
1) Replay traces with current config (baseline).
2) Replay with token_budget relaxed + burst-aware hold-on-prefetch.
3) Replay with hold-on-prefetch + suppress-partial-preempt.
Collect p50/p95, memcpys, kernel-switch count, kv-miss rate.

sam_runtime: I'll put together a minimal patch that implements the hold + sticky-kernel table + suppress-preempt toggle behind a flag. planning to run replay in perf sandbox tomorrow.

carla_eng: if experiments look good we can roll canary with config flag off for 5% of streaming capacity, monitor with dashboard tile (p95, kernel-fallback-rate, nvlink_stalls).

deploy-bot: deploy-requested: branch sam/burst-aware-admission -> perf-sandbox. CI checks: unit, integration, perf-smoke.

sam_runtime: thanks — will push PR with feature flag and perf harness notes.

lina_sre: one more note: partial-decode scheduler has a priority decay that currently resets on every small batch. We should add a decay floor when many preemptions recently observed to avoid priority inversion. I'll file a follow-up ticket after we see replay results. :memo:

sam_runtime: thanks all. I'll paste perf results here after the replay. If replay shows >25% reduction in kernel-switches and p95 down by >20ms, we can start canarying.

miguel_ml: sounds good. cc @carla_eng for canary plan.

carla_eng: got it.
